summary: Build TPM skills to reduce downtime, improve OEE, and strengthen reliability. Enroll for practical tools, templates, and expert-led training.
lede: Total productive maintenance (TPM) helps maintenance and production professionals identify equipment losses and improve reliability. For teams working to stabilize production and reduce chronic downtime, the course develops practical skills in OEE calculation, loss analysis, and autonomous and planned maintenance. Participants also practice root cause failure analysis, equipment inspection routines, maintenance planning, digital inspection workflows, and TPM deployment reporting.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who influence equipment reliability, maintenance execution, and production continuity in asset-intensive operations. Maintenance Managers responsible for TPM deployment and maintenance loss reduction. Reliability Engineers analyzing OEE losses and chronic equipment failure patterns. Production Supervisors coordinating Autonomous Maintenance on the shop floor. Plant Engineers improving maintainability, center lining, and basic equipment conditions. Operations Managers balancing throughput, downtime, and maintenance priorities. Condition Monitoring Specialists using vibration and inspection data for early fault detection. Maintenance Planners and Schedulers optimizing PM work orders and shutdown windows. Quality Engineers linking equipment performance to defect reduction and process stability. Continuous Improvement Leaders embedding TPM pillars into improvement routines. Asset Integrity Coordinators tracking maintenance actions, standards, and escalation logs.
prerequisites: Participants should have experience in manufacturing, utilities, process operations, or asset-intensive environments, along with a working knowledge of equipment performance, maintenance routines, and production loss drivers. Familiarity with OEE, preventive maintenance, and basic root cause analysis will help you move faster, but the course is designed to build TPM capability from operational practice rather than advanced engineering theory. A laptop is recommended for working on templates, dashboards, and action plans. No coding is required. Advanced topics such as predictive maintenance analytics and digital CMMS workflows are covered at an operational level.
